errors.evidence: The figure contains three separate pie charts, not a single pie chart.

errors.text_span: the distribution of problem difficulty levels across four categories: easy, medium, hard, and N+K-.
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly identifies the titles of the three charts ('easy', 'medium', 'hard') as categories (slices) within a single chart. The actual categories, consistent across all three charts, are 'N+K+', 'N-K+', 'N-K-', and 'N+K-'.

errors.text_span: The “easy” slice is green and occupies approximately 45.9%
errors.evidence: There is no 'easy' slice; 'easy' is the title of the first chart. In that chart, the 45.9% slice corresponds to the 'N-K+' category, which is colored yellow, not green.

errors.text_span: the “medium” slice is orange and represents roughly 44.6%
errors.evidence: There is no 'medium' slice; 'medium' is the title of the second chart. In that chart, the 44.6% slice corresponds to the 'N+K+' category, which is colored teal, not orange.

errors.text_span: the “hard” slice is teal and accounts for approximately 36.8%
errors.evidence: There is no 'hard' slice; 'hard' is the title of the third chart. In that chart, the 36.8% slice corresponds to the 'N-K-' category, which is colored peach, not teal.

errors.text_span: the “N+K-” slice is yellow and represents approximately 7.0%
errors.evidence: In the 'hard' chart, the 7.0% value does correspond to the 'N+K-' category, but this slice is colored red, not yellow. The yellow slice represents 'N-K+'.
A legend is clearly visible on the right side of the figure, defining the four categories and their corresponding colors.

errors.text_span: the segments appear to be ordered in descending size from largest to smallest.
errors.evidence: The slices within each pie chart are not ordered by size. For example, in the 'easy' chart, the slice values are 40.6%, 45.9%, 10.1%, and 3.3%, which is not a descending order.
